resolvedFindings.change: Attachment removal completion calls a closure bound to the original draft key, reads its current stored or in-memory content, removes only the deleted ID, and never publishes that state into another selected draft. Draft-change events carry a key, preserving an unrelated storage-denied draft. Regression tests retain edited A text/options, remove A attachment, leave B unchanged, and preserve unsaved B input.

Snapshot item order supplies chronology; full live items remain authoritative. Text with no reliable snapshot/delta boundary is kept in separately labelled historySync sources, avoiding overlap guesses and silent truncation. Full item completion replaces the temporary view. Every turn completion performs a read-only refresh with cleared touched state, covering a missing item-completed event with or without an observed start. Same-thread/epoch diff and token usage survive the refresh. Tests cover repeated text, chronological prefix, full completion, missing completion, final readiness, display labels, and diff/usage retention.

Dispatcher reserves/checks a durable mutation identity before invoking an internal requireConnection callback for new worker work. This preserves accepted/not_sent/unknown/pending/dispatching receipt facts and same-ID fingerprint conflicts without granting an absent or replaced browser owner any fresh worker dispatch. HTTP tests cover all five stored states, changed payloads, no-lease fresh requests, and zero worker calls.

All fetches explicitly send Accept application/json and X-Requested-With XMLHttpRequest. Standard gateway unauthorized envelopes remain distinct from outer authentication failures, including initial session GET. The retained login page offers only its current site URL in a new tab plus an explicit read-only session recheck; no arbitrary Location redirect, automatic mutation replay or page reload is used. Generation guards reject stale 401 invalidation after renewing the same gateway CSRF. Administrator-token rejection retains its specific message for both 400 and 401. The parent supplied the actual proxy behavior; this agent verified the fix with API/application fixtures only.
